questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First and foremost it was important to me, that all the courses I wanted to take were taught in English, and that the university I went to, was of a great quality.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The quality of the courses varied greatly, while some where very challenging, others were almost non-academic (at least after my understanding) 
I did however gain other skills outside of the curriculum, such as video editing and using new software for my assignments, which we don't use at my home university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: If anything NUS almost overloads us with information. The paperwork and the practical stuff was easily managed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Even though I was signed up for a buddy program, I never actually met my buddy (who herself was a 1st year, so probably didn't know much more about the facilities than I.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: All information via email. The physical meetings were primarily social mixers.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any of the accommodations I had applied for, but luckily was offered something else, which was affordable (Sheares Hall).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a mandatory meal plan, which honestly was almost inedible. The cooking facilities were cleaned by the students themselves with no oversight, so it was quite unappealing. And very little fridge space.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Because I lived in housing without air conditioning, I had to have my windows open constantly (not that it made much of a difference), which made the noise from outside more noticeable, quiet hours are not kept or taken seriously, so be prepared to switch your sleep schedule.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quite dirty and dated - rooms really need a make-over.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were one million steps and so many deadlines. For me, it was very confusing. However as an exchange student you are ahead, because of the early deadlines and pre-approvals, where local students seem to register and change courses last minute.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Most of the registration I did from home, which was described in detail by KU Abroad. The registrations in Singapore were primarily about getting your Student Pass (the card that proves you are studying in Singapore and gives you rights as a resident for about a year (I think)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We received a bunch of emails with instructions. Part of the student pass registration was set up on campus, which was very convenient.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check your email every day in the first time in Singapore! You don't want to miss a deadline.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses had little to no theoretic texts to lean on. I studied in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, which is not very revered at NUS

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
MUT1201 was quite challenging (and taught at the YSTCM) most assignments were clear, but with some, the intentions were not clear. 
SE2224 was only focused on the practical part of the course. Very little focus on theory, and with unclear instructions for assignments.
TS2233 Was a very experimenting class, where we in the first part did some very rudimentary exercises, in the second half we were rushed through a creative process, which we were in charge of ourselves.
TS3243 resembled a night class. No academic texts, but we were expected to know theory, even though it was not stated as a pre-requisite to have taken other film-classes, and no reading recommendations were listed or given. The professor's analyses were the correct ones, and challenging her view was not welcome. It ended with a group project, but with no other group exercises during the semester, I ended up in a group with total strangers, or student who don't show up to class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was no specific style of teaching at NUS, but rather the teaching method varied depending on the professors. They each had their own methods and levels of commitment. I could write an essay about each professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Classical Music Composition 
Unmasked! An introduction to Dance in SEA
Making Contemporary Performances
Stage and Screen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Classical Music Composition: The professor knew her stuff, the exercises and examples stretched beyond the Classical and she had suggestions for independent exercises and was very flexible when it came to consultation times if we were unable to attend in the allotted time slots. 
Unmasked! An Introduction to Dance in SEA: Because there is a field trip to Bali (a bit expensive though) and you get to perform a big show. It is a physically challenging class, but also very fun.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You need money for visiting all the amazing countries surrounding Singapore :)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Foods with vegetables is expensive! And so is alcohol... 
Taking the MRT or the bus is very cheap (compared to Danish costs)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
They have amazing sports fascinates! USE THEM
It is difficult to join clubs when you are only here for one semester though

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything - from fencing to mountaineering and martial arts to sailing. There are more than a hundred student clubs I think. The halls (accommodations) also have their own activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of their amazing sports facilities and use this opportunity to develop new skills! I took a sailing course for 250 SGD and can now sail a dinghy :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Singapore is the Dubai of Asia. There are some amazing malls, but the cultural experiences are limited.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not very difficult. Show up on time (no academic 15 minutes) and make sure to look up! Singaporeans look into their phones when they walk haha

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Strike up a conversation in the mid class break. Start out with talking about the class. Or join the open meetings in the student clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Singaporeans mostly keep to themselves - like most Danes do. Touching and even eye contact is considered somewhat intimate. I bought a stuffed animal at the Oceanarium to cuddle haha. Beware of the climate. it is hot and humid!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The "You can do it!" attitude during exams. Our dining hall was turned into a study area late at night during exam period - where they turned on the airconditioning and we were given a goody bag with snacks. Snacks is the love language here! And stickers!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Focus on LEARNING! Our grades are not transferred, only pass/fail status. Focus on gaining new skills and experiencing the culture. I wish I had spent more time exploring, even though I have been to many places and done many things - there was room for more! And when making friends, don't wait for others to make the first move. Be bold, and sit next to someone you don't know and introduce yourself - but maybe wait for them to open a conversation. And find a method to remember names!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are free buses driving around on campus. Use them - walking is not worth it, you will get to class all sweaty

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the extra skills I have learned and some of the connections I have made - especially with other exchange students from other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: You will sometimes feel a bit isolated. And the heat

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Time passes quickly! Suddenly it's time to go home and you missed out on things. Always say yes!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
